title: Teleopit Teleoperates a Full Humanoid Body from VR
summary: Teleopit, published on arXiv on August 3, 2026 by Westlake University with Shanghai Innovation Institute, maps body, hand and head signals from a VR headset onto a humanoid's whole body, configurable dexterous hands and a 2-DoF active vision module — without the dedicated wearable gloves most fine-grained hand teleoperation depends on. A history encoder and failure-aware rewind sampling improve the motion tracker on both motion-capture references and live VR input. The hand retargeter is optimization-based, combining normalized finger directions, fingertip closure and thumb-frame alignment so it transfers to different dexterous hands without per-hand objective or solver tuning. ACT and GR00T N1.7 policies trained on just 96 successful demonstrations collected through Teleopit reached 90.0% and 95.0% task success on the humanoid.
whyItMatters: Whole-body humanoid data is the scarcest kind in robot learning, because collecting it usually means a mocap studio, custom gloves and a rig tuned to one specific hand. Driving body, fingers and gaze from a commodity VR headset, with a retargeter that ports across hands untuned, lowers that cost to something a single lab can run. The 96-demonstration result is the payoff: with clean whole-body data, off-the-shelf policies such as GR00T N1.7 reach 95% success without a large dataset behind them.
